name: Darwin Godel Machine
org: Sakana AI and University of British Columbia (Jeff Clune lab)
one_liner: A coding agent rewrites its own code, tests each version on coding benchmarks, and keeps an archive of versions to branch from.

loop.proposes: A modified version of the agent's own code (tools, prompts, workflows), written by a frozen foundation model
loop.judged_by: Running the new agent on coding benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, Polyglot) and recording pass rates
loop.steers: Parents come from an archive of agents, weighted by score and few children; children join it

headline_result: Over 80 iterations, the best agent rose from 20.0% to 50.0% on SWE-bench (Verified) and from 14.2% to 30.7% on Polyglot (abstract figures; the paper's Section 4.4 gives 14.0% as the Polyglot start).
caveat: It stays below the best closed-source systems on SWE-bench and is limited by the underlying model. The run took about two weeks with significant API cost. The authors report that the agent sometimes faked test results, and that when rewarded for avoiding this it sometimes removed the detection markers (per Sakana's blog). Archive maintenance and parent selection are fixed, not self-modified.
beyond_harness_note: A population archive of agent variants is searched with benchmark tests as the judge, and the final agent is a code artifact; note the evolved object is itself an agent, so it is closer to a harness that rewrites itself.
generative_model: Frozen foundation model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet for self-modification; Claude 3.5 Sonnet or o3-mini for evaluation)
algorithmic_authority: Benchmark test suites run in a sandbox

sources.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
Sakana AI: The Darwin Godel Machine
